title: Marguerite and the Witness
premise: Orsen Marchetti, the observant concierge of the Hotel Verlaine who has quietly solved three deaths the police dismissed as accidents, is hired by a nervous stranger named Aldous Wren to prove that his sister Vivienne will not be murdered — a crime he insists has not yet happened. As Orsen investigates, she discovers Vivienne is heir to a contested estate built on a death thirty years ago, and every alibi protecting the family was woven the night of that original 'accident.' When Vivienne dies anyway despite Orsen's warnings, she realizes Wren's real purpose: he needed a witness no one would suspect to expose the killer before the statute of inheritance closes. In the end, Orsen turns the hotel itself into a trap, forcing a confession on its recorded switchboard and reclaiming her own buried memory of the night thirty years ago — for Orsen's mother was the first victim.
about_author: Mirabel Dravenmoor spent a decade working night desks in grand European hotels, collecting the small cruelties and kindnesses of strangers. She writes mysteries about people who see too much and are believed too little.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Orsen Marchetti's POV. A trembling man named Aldous Wren books a room and pays Orsen privately to prevent a murder that hasn't happened yet — his sister Vivienne's. Orsen, who solved three 'accidents' from behind the front desk, takes the retainer against her better judgment. Emotional beat: wary curiosity sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Vivienne Arrives
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Vivienne Wren checks in with two lawyers and a locked attaché case, claiming she's here to settle her late father's estate. Orsen maps the party's rooms, habits, and hostilities. Beat: the pleasure of pattern-reading curdling as she counts three people with motives already forming.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibi
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with a flashback fragment. Digging through archives, Orsen finds the origin: Vivienne's uncle drowned at the family's lakeside lodge in 1994, ruled an accident, leaving the fortune to Vivienne's father. Every surviving relative has an alibi for that night — too polished, too identical. Beat: unease.

chapters.title: The Concierge Knows Everything
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Using keys, laundry schedules, and telephone logs, Orsen learns someone searched Vivienne's room. Suspicion falls on the younger lawyer, Caspian Hale, but the evidence feels planted. Wren grows evasive when she asks why he didn't go to police. Beat: frustration and first doubt of her client.

chapters.title: A Death Postponed
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Vivienne reveals she knows someone means to kill her; the attaché case holds proof of who really killed her uncle thirty years ago. She trusts no one — least of all the watchful concierge. Beat: fear braided with defiance; the reader sees what Orsen cannot.

chapters.title: The Second Accident
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The elder lawyer, Margot Sennet, falls down the service stairs hours after meeting Vivienne alone. Police call it drink. Orsen calls it method — identical to the 1994 drowning's staging. Beat: cold recognition that the killer is following an old script.

chapters.title: What the Switchboard Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Old hotel records show a call placed from the lodge the night of the 1994 death — to this very hotel, room 412, then occupied by a name Orsen half-recognizes. Her hands shake reading it. Beat: memory pressing at a door she keeps locked.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Aldous Wren's POV. Wren admits he wasn't told about the murder by chance: an anonymous letter promised him the truth if he brought Vivienne here. He withheld this from Orsen out of shame. Beat: guilt; the reader now doubts whether Wren is protector or bait.

chapters.title: The Family Portrait
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen gathers the heirs: cousins Odile and Tomas Ferrand, both named in the uncle's will before it was rewritten. Their alibis for 1994 match word for word — rehearsed. One of them flinches when Orsen mentions room 412. Beat: tightening net, rising menace.

chapters.title: Locked Case, Opened
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen picks the attaché lock and finds only a photograph: the lodge, 1994, five figures — including a hotel employee she recognizes as her own young mother. Beat: vertigo; the mystery and Orsen's past fuse into one thread.

chapters.title: The Night Orsen Forgot
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, extended flashback. Recovering suppressed memory: nine-year-old Orsen watched from the lodge stairwell as her mother made a midnight phone call — and later died in a fire ruled accidental. The hotel where she works was her mother's employer. Beat: grief detonating into resolve.

chapters.title: Three Deaths, One Hand
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen lays out her old cases and sees the signature: each 'accident' silenced a witness to 1994. Her mother was the first. The killer has been pruning witnesses for thirty years, and Vivienne's evidence makes her the last branch. Beat: terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Vivienne Disappears
chapters.summary: Aldous Wren's POV. Wren wakes to find Vivienne gone, her room staged like a departure but her coat left behind. He panics and finally tells Orsen everything, begging forgiveness. Beat: dread; the race becomes a rescue.

chapters.title: The Lodge
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Following freight records, Orsen traces a car to the shuttered family lodge. Inside: signs of struggle, Vivienne's blood, and the 1994 evidence hidden in the boathouse — letters proving the uncle was murdered over the will. Beat: horror and urgency.

chapters.title: Caspian's Bargain
chapters.summary: Caspian Hale's POV. The young lawyer, cornered by Orsen, confesses he was paid to steal Vivienne's evidence — by Margot Sennet, before her fall. He doesn't know who employs him ultimately, but gives a name: the estate's executor, Silas Renner. Beat: betrayal within betrayal.

chapters.title: Room 412
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen confronts the past: the 1994 call came to the hotel manager of that era — Silas Renner, still employed, now the estate's trusted executor and the man who reported her mother's fire. He has been inside every death since. Beat: icy shock.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Sprung
chapters.summary: Silas Renner's POV. Renner, elegant and unrepentant, has kept Vivienne alive because the will requires her living signature — for one more day. He explains, almost tenderly, how accidents are made. Orsen, hiding in the hotel's old dumbwaiter shaft, hears everything. Beat: villain revealed; clock ticking.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen persuades the skeptical inspector Lachaire with her three prior solutions and the boathouse letters, then rigs the hotel's vintage switchboard to record. She must make Renner confess while keeping Vivienne alive until she signs. Beat: taut preparation, quiet courage.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Held in the hotel's sealed attic suite, Vivienne stalls Renner with legalities, buying hours. She signs — but signs the wrong page deliberately, buying more time. Beat: nerve; the hunted becomes a player.

chapters.title: Confession on Tape
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen baits Renner with the one thing he can't resist: proof his 1994 call survived. Believing himself safe, he describes how he drowned the uncle and burned Orsen's mother — while the switchboard reels turn. Lachaire's men close in. Beat: cathartic reversal.

chapters.title: What Inheritance Means
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Renner, undone, tries one last 'accident' in custody and fails. The estate passes to Vivienne, who funds a memorial for the forgotten victims — including Orsen's mother, publicly cleared after thirty years. Beat: mourning transmuted into justice.

chapters.title: The Next Guest
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue. Orsen returns to the desk, changed but unchanged, her mother's photograph beside the bell. A new guest lingers at the counter with a question that sounds like the beginning of another story. Orsen notices everything. Beat: quiet restoration, door left ajar.
